permissions_impact: Original/renewed initial receipt replay retains current actor, web-session proof, ledger scope/field and source checks. No user grants, hooks or public endpoint; existing flags stay default-disabled and release evidence writes stay closed.
migration_impact: No new model, column or index in this slice. Depends on prior six release scope columns and reviewed indexes; no maintained server migration or automatic backfill.
rollback_plan: Revert receipt reader changes while retaining all immutable roots/events/confirmations and encrypted receipts. Older code rejects legitimate released histories, so retain compatible full-history reads before enabling release writes; never delete evidence.
security_impact: Completed original/renewed initial requests may replay their existing encrypted result only after a fresh full purchase inspection acquires common source/budget guards and verifies complete independent original, renewal and release evidence. The selected current position is re-read with an exact bounded physical event count and compared to the inspected position; each tail independently loads its release confirmation/decision. Original event identity, all frozen root/document fields, original actor/session proof and current source/role/scope are rechecked. Original receipts reject any renewal successor. A guard already held at entry grants no released-history replay: that path still accepts exactly one initial event. Historical validity never authorizes a new write or extends proof expiry. Missing, extra, stale, substituted or tampered facts fail closed and outer verifiers poison the guard/full transaction. No controller, table, public API, hook or role is opened. New tests append release facts only to connection-private copies and use synthetic sessions/confirmations; they do not establish a real human release, release-write atomicity, noncooperating writers or hospital capacity.
